silent_decisions.operation: load the raw crowdstorming dataset from CSV as the analysis source
drop every row with any missing value before building the working sample
restrict analysis to a random draw of 250 referees rather than the full referee pool
z-score every model covariate (skin tone, height, weight, goals, IAT, experience) before fitting
fit an alternate red-card model on the full unsampled data using rater1's raw rating treated as a categorical factor, with a player random intercept
refit the same rater1 model but treat the rating as a continuous linear predictor instead of a factor
swap in rater2's categorical rating in place of rater1 for the same model structure
build two alternate skin-tone measures by taking the elementwise min (lower) and max (higher) of the two raters' scores
fit the red-card model using the min-of-two-raters score as the skin-tone predictor
fit the red-card model using the max-of-two-raters score as the skin-tone predictor

misalignments.decision: fit a poisson GLMM for red cards on height, weight, goals and position with a referee random intercept, holding skin tone out entirely
misalignments.claim: a multilevel logistic regression model was used to analyze data on male soccer players in top European divisions
misalignments.note: claim states a multilevel logistic regression was used, but decision 8 fits a Poisson GLMM
